chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"No one is prohibited [from eating the game] while he has something of the game with him, until he removes it from his possession. If he brings it into the Sanctuary, it becomes obligatory upon him to release it. If he does not do so, and he enters the Sanctuary and dies, the redemption [compensation] becomes incumbent upon him."
ai.seo_question: What happens to game caught by a pilgrim if they die inside the Haram boundaries?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the transitional status of game caught by a pilgrim, establishing that prohibition is not immediate but contingent upon entering the Haram boundaries. It highlights the legal principle that if the animal is retained within the sacred precincts at the time of death, the compensation (Fida') becomes a debt upon the estate, reflecting the juristic view that the sanctity of the space triggers the obligation. This ruling underscores the practical implications for pilgrims managing their possessions during the ritual state of Ihram.
